home.name: Francis Desjardins
home.breathing: Infrastructure engineer — building blocks, client side and server side · Breathing air since 1980.
home.enough: Prefers explicit over implicit, predictable over magical. Writes primitives other people build things with — which is either very useful or very humbling depending on the day. What a library refuses to do is the first decision, not the last.

skills.title: What I build
skills.description: Framework-free cores with thin bindings over them. The core is plain TypeScript that runs in a browser, a worker or a service, and the binding is the only part that knows which — a test walks the import graph and fails if the core ever reaches a framework. Zero runtime dependencies, three for three.
skills.thinking: The same habits either side of the wire: derive behaviour from what was declared instead of adding a flag for it, write the refusals down before the features, and put a gate where a convention would otherwise be a comment nobody re-reads. Measures things in nanoseconds when nobody is watching.
skills.secondary: Also: a self-declared cat person. No further questions.

work.title: What's running
work.description: Three pieces, each with a surface you can try. The names come from the shadows an eclipse casts. What they refuse to do is documented as carefully as the rest.

dialog.name: antumbra
dialog.description: Dialog manager on the native top layer. Zero shipped UI: the renderer stays yours. React, Solid and vanilla bindings.

boot.name: umbra
boot.description: Bootstrap orchestration, and not a front-end kind: the core needs no DOM, so one declared graph boots a page, a worker or a service. You say what each step needs; the parallelism is derived from that — no flag, no concurrency ceiling.

designSystem.name: penumbra
designSystem.description: The design system all three playgrounds wear — and the page that takes it apart, one layer at a time.
